plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single name mandate.
Add to QQQI, bringing it to 25% of the book, favoring income and broad index exposure.
Buy ZS for 5% of the book, adding a top-quality name from the scanner.
This plan aims for capital preservation and a large cash buffer.
conservative.read: This conservative plan targets a modest ~1.5%/month return, prioritizing capital preservation. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and lowering concentration. Expect lower volatility and drawdowns, but also more limited upside potential.

plan: Trim SOXL to 3% and SPAL to 2% to reduce leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 25% to meet the single name concentration mandate.
Buy ZS for 4% of the book, adding a high-scoring quality tech name.
Buy PANW for 4% of the book, adding another high-scoring quality tech name.
This plan balances broad index exposure with quality tech and reduced leverage.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets ~2.5%/month, focusing on risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while blending broad index exposure with quality tech. Expect moderate volatility and drawdowns, with reasonable growth potential.

plan: Add to SOXL, bringing it to 6%, and SPAL to 6%, increasing leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 25% to meet the single name mandate and free up capital.
Buy ZS for 6% of the book, concentrating in a high-scoring scanner setup.
Buy PANW for 6% of the book, concentrating in another high-scoring scanner setup.
This plan stretches for growth by using leverage and concentrating in strong setups.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4%/month, aiming for stretch growth. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and concentrates in high-scoring setups. Be aware this raises both upside and drawdown potential; leveraged ETFs decay daily, and this mode can lose a lot fast if stops are not strictly adhered to.

plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and reallocate.
Add to QQQI, bringing it to 30% of the book, rotating into an income ETF.
Buy GGLL for 5% of the book, adding another name for potential yield and lower beta.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly distributions and low drawdown.
income.read: This income plan targets ~1%/month, aiming to park cash for yield. It rotates heavily into income/covered-call ETFs and broad index, cutting high-beta names. While prioritizing low drawdown and reliable income, distributions are variable and NAV can still fall in a selloff; this is not a savings account.
